title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 385 (Fee for registration of documents)

content.overview: There shall be paid to the Registrar for registering any document required by the provisions of this Chapter to be registered by him, such fee as may be prescribed.
content.glance: Prescribed fee is payable to the Registrar for registering any document required under Chapter XXII.
content.study: Section 385 is a short fee provision. Any document that Chapter XXII requires the Registrar to register attracts the prescribed fee. Non-payment leaves the delivery incomplete for registration purposes.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: A prescribed fee is payable to the Registrar for registering any document required under Chapter XXII.

examples.title: Illustration — s. 385
examples.body: A foreign company delivers s. 380 documents and pays the prescribed registration fee under s. 385.

hypotheticals.question: What is the core effect of s. 385?
hypotheticals.analysis: It requires payment of the prescribed fee for registration of Chapter XXII documents by the Registrar.

rows.left: Fee for registration of Chapter XXII documents

misconceptions.trap: Assuming delivery without fee completes registration.
misconceptions.correction: s. 385 requires payment of the prescribed fee for registration by the Registrar.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should s. 385 be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the Chapter XXII document. II. Confirm the prescribed fee. III. Conclude on registration completeness.
